Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City

amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-51 – BUDGET AMENDMENT FOR ANNUAL WATER

Background:

The California Department of Water Resources (DWR) requires urban retail water suppliers to
submit an Annual Water Loss Report for every calendar year to be in compliance with Senate
Bill (SB) 555 adopted in 2015. The annual water loss report provides a systematic approach to
auditing and managing water loss in the water distribution system. The report’s results help
increase water supplies and recover revenues by identifying the scale and cost of these losses.

Arcadis, Inc. (Arcadis) has been assisting the City in the preparation and validation of its water
loss reports from calendar year (CY) 2016 to CY 2022. The last Annual Water Loss Report for
CY 2021 was completed in September 2022. On February 14, 2024 under the City Manager’s
authority, the City approved an agreement with Arcadis to update the CY 2022, CY 2023, and
CY 2024 Annual Water Loss Reports over a three-year term. The professional services provided
by Arcadis assists the City with DWR regulatory compliance requirements.

New and more complex reporting requirements from DWR have resulted in additional technical
review to ensure the quality of data and documentation. To maintain compliance and ensure
the City is reporting the most accurate data available, staff is recommending a review of past
reports. The audit could result in improved scores for the City’s water distribution system and
reduced compliance requirements in the future.

Staff requested a proposal from Arcadis to perform an audit review on Annual Water Loss
Reports submitted for previous CYs. The work scope (major tasks) for Annual Water Loss

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-52 SUPPORTING PROPOSITION 36

Background:

Proposition 36, one of the ten propositions on the November 2024 ballot, aims to create tougher
penalties for serial theft and smash-and-grabs, confront the fentanyl crisis in our communities,
and incentivize drug and mental health treatment. It is supported by a coalition of Democrats,
Independents, Republicans, small businesses, local elected leaders, law enforcement, social
justice organizations, and crime victims’ and drug survivor advocates.

Since the passage of Prop 47 ten years ago, California has seen an increase in property crimes
and homelessness. Prop 36 attempts to walk back some of these unintentional consequences.
It will allow felony charges for possessing certain drugs and for thefts under $950 with two prior
drug or two prior theft convictions, as applications. For defendants who plead guilty to felony
drug possession, they can be ordered to undergo a new treatment-focused court process.
Additionally, Prop 36 will ensure that fentanyl is treated similarly to heroin, cocaine, PCP and
methamphetamines when offenders possess a firearm. Lastly, Prop 36 will require courts to
warn individuals convicted of selling or providing certain drugs that they could be charged with
murder if they sell or provide illegal drugs that kill someone, such as fentanyl. Prop 36 will
strengthen laws to help reduce crime, and help provide greater safety for our communities.

Therefore, Resolution No. 24-52 has been prepared for City Council consideration to support
Proposition 36.

SUBJECT:  ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (4), Community Promotion
(1), Historical Heritage (5), International Friendship Commission (4), Public Safety (1), Senior
Citizens (1), and the Youth Commission (all 15). The Youth Commission does not have any
members at this time. The age range for the Youth Commission is between 13 to 18 years of
age. Each City Councilmember has three appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Any
Councilmember may nominate an individual who falls into one of the two categories:
Business/Community College Representative and at-large Community Representative.

The International Friendship Commission has not met since 2009, but recently an appointment
was made with the intent of re-establishing it. In 2005, the City officially ended its relationship
with Hermosillo and Fresnillo by adopting Resolution No. 05-33; and established a new
relationship with Morelia, Michoacan, Mexico by adopting Resolution No. 05-34. According to
Resolution No. 20-61, Advisory Body procedures, the International Friendship Commission shall
have the following purposes:
